title: Antenatal schedule and ongoing assessment
blurb: Plan 10 or 7 appointments by parity, know what happens at each contact, measure and plot fundal height, and check presentation from 36 weeks.
question: Leila is 31 weeks pregnant with her first baby and has an uncomplicated pregnancy. Her parous friend did not have a 31-week appointment. Why does Leila have one, and what should the midwife do at it?

teach.body: NICE NG201 plans 10 routine antenatal appointments for nulliparous women (no previous birth) and 7 for parous women (at least one previous birth). First-time mothers have three extra contacts, at 25, 31 and 40 weeks, for more information and support. Every contact is a fresh assessment, not just a check: the midwife asks about wellbeing, measures, reviews the plan and decides whether extra care is needed (SPM 3.23).

items.label: Results; reassess PE and FGR risk
Bloods, anti-D if RhD-negative, RSV vaccine
If not given birth: sweep, induction

teach.caption: Either group can have extra or longer appointments if her medical, social or emotional needs require (NG201 1.1.10).

head: Check
Detail
rows: Validated device; refer if 140/90 or more after 20 wks
General health, concerns, safe chance to talk
Review and reassess; identify extra care
teach.caption: NG201 1.2.10, 1.2.11, 1.2.24, 1.2.28, 1.2.30, 1.2.34.

teach.body: From 24+0 weeks, measure symphysis fundal height (SFH) at each appointment, no more often than every 2 weeks, and plot it on a growth chart; the first measurement should be by 28+6 (SBL v3). If SFH suggests a small baby, offer a growth scan; if large, consider one. Stop SFH once serial growth scans start. Uncomplicated singleton pregnancies are not routinely scanned after 28 weeks.

Leila is nulliparous, so 31 weeks is one of her three extra contacts. The midwife asks how she is and about her baby's movements, checks BP with a validated device, tests urine for protein, and measures SFH, plotting it on Leila's chart. It has dropped from the line at 28 weeks, so she offers a growth scan rather than waiting. She updates the records and talks through preparing for labour, as NG201 suggests after 28 weeks.

teach.text: Parous means she has given birth before; it is parity, not gravidity, that sets 7 versus 10 visits. And SFH is measured no more often than every 2 weeks: a worrying measurement leads to a scan, not a remeasure next week.

items: Every visit: BP (validated device), urine for protein, wellbeing and safety questions, review the plan, update records.
From 24+0: ask about fetal movements and measure SFH (no more than 2-weekly, first by 28+6), plotted on a chart.
Small SFH: offer a growth scan. No routine scans after 28 weeks in uncomplicated singleton pregnancies.
From 36+0: palpate for presentation; suspected breech confirmed by scan; offer ECV for uncomplicated breech.
From 38 weeks discuss prolonged pregnancy; at 41 weeks offer sweep and discuss induction.

summary: You can now set out the NG201 schedule for nulliparous and parous women, carry out the core checks at every contact, measure and act on fundal height, and manage presentation from 36 weeks. You can also tell which visits exist for first-time mothers only.

A.q: How many routine antenatal appointments does NICE NG201 plan for a nulliparous woman with an uncomplicated pregnancy?
A.why: NG201 1.1.7: plan 10 routine appointments for nulliparous women (7 for parous women).

whyNot.0: 7 is the number for parous women.

A.q: Which of these routine appointments is offered to nulliparous women but not to parous women?
A.why: The extra nulliparous appointments are at 25, 31 and 40 weeks.

whyNot.0: 28 weeks is offered to all women (bloods, anti-D).
whyNot.2: 34 weeks is offered to all women.
whyNot.3: 36 weeks is offered to all women.

A.q: From what gestation should symphysis fundal height be measured at antenatal appointments?
A.why: NG201 1.2.30 and SBL v3: measure SFH at each appointment after 24+0 weeks, with the first by 28+6.

whyNot.0: 16 weeks is too early for routine SFH.
whyNot.1: 20 weeks is earlier than the NICE start point.
whyNot.2: 28+0 is too late to start; the first must be by 28+6, starting from 24+0.

B.q: Which checks should be carried out at every routine face-to-face antenatal appointment?
B.why: NG201 1.2.24 and 1.2.28: measure BP with a validated device and offer a urine dipstick for proteinuria at every routine face-to-face appointment.

whyNot.1: FBC is checked at booking and 28 weeks, not every visit.
whyNot.2: Glucose challenge testing is not used for GDM risk.
whyNot.3: Fasting glucose is not a routine every-visit test.

B.q: At 36+2 weeks, the midwife suspects breech presentation on palpation. What is the next step?
options: Offer an ultrasound to confirm presentation
B.why: NG201 1.2.37: if breech is suspected on palpation, offer a scan to determine presentation; if confirmed and uncomplicated, discuss options including ECV.

whyNot.0: Options are discussed after confirmation; ECV is offered first for uncomplicated breech.
whyNot.2: Presentation should be confirmed by scan before ECV.
whyNot.3: Waiting loses time to offer ECV.

B.q: Ama has had one baby before and has an uncomplicated pregnancy. Which appointment is NOT part of her routine schedule?
B.why: Parous women have 7 routine appointments; 25, 31 and 40 weeks are extra contacts for nulliparous women.

whyNot.0: 28 weeks is offered to all women.
whyNot.1: 34 weeks is offered to all women.
whyNot.3: 38 weeks is offered to all women.

C.q: At 31 weeks, Leila's SFH plots well below the curve set by her measurements at 25 and 28 weeks. She reports normal movements and her BP is normal. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Remeasure the SFH in one week
Reassure, as SFH varies between women
Offer an ultrasound for fetal growth
C.why: NG201 1.2.32: if SFH suggests a small-for-gestational-age baby, offer a scan for fetal growth and wellbeing.

whyNot.0: SFH should be measured no more often than every 2 weeks; a concern needs a scan.
whyNot.1: A falling trajectory is a concern, not normal variation.
whyNot.2: Delaying the scan to 36 weeks could miss growth restriction.

C.q: Rosa, 32 weeks, has an uncomplicated singleton pregnancy. She asks for a routine growth scan to check the baby's size. What is the best response?
options: Book a growth scan for 34 weeks
Explain SFH is used; routine scans are not
Book a scan at 36 weeks for presentation
C.why: NG201 1.2.33: do not routinely offer scans after 28 weeks in uncomplicated singleton pregnancies; growth is monitored by plotted SFH.

whyNot.0: A routine scan is not indicated without a concern.
whyNot.1: Serial scans are for women with raised FGR risk.
whyNot.3: Presentation is checked by palpation; a scan follows only if breech is suspected.

C.q: Hana, nulliparous, is at her 41-week appointment and has not given birth. Her pregnancy is uncomplicated. What should the midwife offer?
options: A membrane sweep and a discussion of induction
A plan to induce at 39 weeks next time
C.why: Sweeps are offered at antenatal visits after 39+0 weeks (NG207 1.3.2), and induction is discussed from 41+0 weeks (NG207 1.2.4).

whyNot.1: NICE advises discussing induction from 41+0, not waiting without review.
whyNot.2: Caesarean is not offered for an uncomplicated prolonged pregnancy.
whyNot.3: This does not address her current pregnancy.

reteach.title: Seven for all, three for first-timers
reteach.question: What is the easiest way to remember the two schedules?

blocks.body: Every woman has 7: booking, 16, 28, 34, 36, 38 and 41 (if still pregnant). First-time mothers add 3: 25, 31 and 40, giving 10. At every visit: BP, urine protein, wellbeing, plan, records. From 24 weeks add movements and SFH; from 36 weeks add presentation.

blocks.text: No routine scans after 28 weeks for uncomplicated singletons: plotted SFH does the job.

explain.body: Nulliparous: 10 routine appointments. Parous: 7. The extra three for nulliparous women are at 25, 31 and 40 weeks.

test.q: How many routine antenatal appointments does NG201 plan for a parous woman?
test.why: NG201 1.1.8: plan 7 routine appointments for parous women.

whyNot.3: 10 is the number for nulliparous women.

explain.body: Ask about health and concerns, give a safe chance to discuss abuse or mental health, check BP with a validated device, dipstick urine for protein, review the care plan and update the records.

test.q: What is the urine dipstick at routine antenatal appointments used to look for?
test.why: NG201 1.2.28: offer a urine dipstick test for proteinuria at every routine appointment, as part of pre-eclampsia surveillance.

whyNot.0: Urine glucose is not used for GDM assessment.
whyNot.1: Ketones are not the routine target.
whyNot.3: Leucocytes are not the routine target of the antenatal dipstick.

explain.body: SFH from 24+0, at most every 2 weeks, plotted, first by 28+6. Small: offer a scan. Large: consider a scan. No routine scans after 28 weeks in uncomplicated singleton pregnancies.

test.q: How often may SFH be measured at most?
test.why: NG201 1.2.30: SFH at each appointment after 24+0, but no more frequently than every 2 weeks.

whyNot.0: Weekly measurement is more frequent than NICE allows.
whyNot.2: Appointments can be 2-weekly; 4 weeks is not the limit.
whyNot.3: This is far more frequent than NICE allows.

explain.body: Palpate for presentation at every appointment after 36+0; confirm suspected breech by scan; offer ECV for uncomplicated breech. From 38 weeks discuss prolonged pregnancy; sweeps from 39+0; induction discussed from 41+0.

test.q: From when should abdominal palpation for presentation be offered at every appointment?
test.why: NG201 1.2.36: offer abdominal palpation at all appointments after 36+0 to identify possible breech presentation.

whyNot.0: 28 weeks is too early; babies often turn later.
whyNot.1: 32 weeks is earlier than the NICE start.
whyNot.2: 34 weeks is earlier than the NICE start.
